title: ROAX conformance corpus v1
description: Schema for the shared cross-language test-vector file. Because ROAX may ship five independent libraries and cannot lean on a single core behind an FFI layer the way dogtag does (spec section 14.3), this corpus is the entire enforcement mechanism for cross-language agreement, not a safety net. Normative content requirements: docs/conformance-corpus.md. The corpus file itself does not exist yet.

corpusVersion.description: Version of this corpus file. The three-part semver pattern is KEPT on purpose: this is one of ROAX's OWN artifacts, so this project defines the identifier and may constrain its shape (spec section 12.1). Every EXTERNALLY defined version in this file is opaque instead - see unicodeVersion below and recordVector.schemaVersion.

hashAlg.description: The hash algorithm these vectors were produced under. It is not merely a label: it is appended to the domain string, which is ASCII 'ROAX-CANON/1/' + hashAlg and sits in every leaf preimage, so every expected hash in this file is specific to it (spec sections 8 and 7.4). It no longer sits in a salt preimage, because decision D4 was ruled D4b and salt derivation is gone (spec section 7.1); the domain string itself is unchanged. Matches the envelope enum deliberately. Only SHA-256 has a construction DEFINED by ROAX-CANON/1; Poseidon-BN254 is registered but its parameterization is not yet pinned, so no Poseidon corpus can exist until a revision pins it (spec section 7.4). STATED LIMIT: the enum deliberately still accepts Poseidon-BN254, mirroring the envelope, so 'no Poseidon corpus can exist' is enforced by the corpus build refusing to produce one rather than by this keyword. There is nothing to enforce structurally yet, because a Poseidon corpus has no expected values to be wrong about until the parameterization is pinned.

unicodeVersion.description: The Unicode version whose NFC tables the expected values were produced under. ROAX-CANON/1 pins 15.1, and '15.1' is the canonical form for this pin (spec section 6.1). An implementation running different tables MAY legitimately differ on vectors in the 'unicodeVersion' class, and must say so rather than silently passing. STATED LIMIT: that is an obligation on the implementation's conformance REPORT, not on this file, so nothing here can enforce it; conformance class 16 owns it and is explicit that it detects a version mismatch by declaration rather than by demonstration. OPAQUE: the Unicode Consortium defines this identifier, not this project, so it carries no shape constraint (spec section 12.1). The earlier two-part pattern rejected '15.1.0', which is the official Unicode Standard version string for the very release being pinned. Widened rather than made a const, because a const would foreclose a future re-pin and the corpus is versioned independently of the specification.

classRef.description: Which numbered class in docs/conformance-corpus.md this vector discharges. Every class must be reachable from at least one vector; a class with no vectors is a coverage gap and the corpus build MUST report it. The maximum tracks the class count stated in section 3 of that document and MUST move with it. Raised from 17 to 19 on 2026-07-28 when the ten engineering decisions were ruled: class 18 fails an implementation that treats an outside-the-root field as authority (decision D8) and class 19 asserts NFC end to end with a root (decision D12). Class numbers are stable - class 12 kept its number and its subject when decision D4 was ruled D4b and lost only its mechanism, so nothing renumbered. THREE DEFINITIONS PIN THEIR CLASS MORE TIGHTLY THAN THIS RANGE, and they are listed here because this is where the coupling note belongs: unlinkabilityVector is const 12, normalizationVector is const 19, and envelopeVector is 13 to 18. Adding a class therefore means checking four places in this file, not one, plus section 3 of docs/conformance-corpus.md. The pins are worth that cost because a mislabelled vector marks the class it names as covered while testing nothing about it, which is the silently-vacuous-vector failure this file guards in several other places.

tagRef.description: A ROAX type tag (spec section 6.1): 0 NULL, 1 BOOL, 2 STRING, 3 INTEGER, 4 DECIMAL, 5 BYTES, 6 EMPTY_ARRAY, 7 EMPTY_OBJECT, 8 BLOB_REF. Tag 8 is REGISTERED and selected by no version-1 profile (spec section 6.5). THIS SCHEMA DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RESTRICT WHERE TAG 8 MAY APPEAR, and that is not an oversight to be closed later: pinning the carrier form once, before five implementations exist, is the reason the tag is defined now, so an encodeValue vector that fixes the encoded bytes of a BLOB_REF value is legitimate and wanted. What spec section 6.5 forbids is narrower than the tag's presence - a type map binding a path to it, and an envelope carrying a tag-8 leaf - so the conforming ISSUANCE-shaped vector carrying it today is the class-11 typeMap vector asserting that such a map is rejected. Schema-valid is deliberately not the same as issuable here, exactly as Poseidon-BN254 is registered in the hashAlg enum and forbidden in issuance. Widened from 7 to 8 when decision D9 was ruled.

carrierValue.description: A record value in CARRIER form, as it is written into a vector file. A JSON NUMBER IS UNREPRESENTABLE HERE, at any depth, and that is the one constraint in this schema that guards the load-bearing invariant of the whole project: a number is never parsed through a float (docs/decisions.md part 0, spec section 6.4). It was prose on two carriers and absent on two others until this was noticed. The failure it prevents is worse than an invalid vector, because it happens before any implementation is involved: a vector written as 0.010 is destroyed by the runner's own JSON parser into 0.01, and the corpus then certifies five independent libraries as agreeing on a DECIMAL trailing-zero premise the file format had already thrown away (spec section 6.2, FHIR R4 SHALL). INTEGER and DECIMAL therefore travel as canonical strings, and so does BLOB_REF's blobByteLength, which is a hash-preimage input for the same reason (spec section 6.5). THIS DUPLICATES NO PER-TAG MAPPING: walking the per-tag allOf conditionals of schemas/envelope-1.0.json shows that no tag carries a JSON number under any of them - BOOL is a boolean, STRING, INTEGER, DECIMAL and BYTES are strings, BLOB_REF is an object of two strings, and NULL, EMPTY_ARRAY and EMPTY_OBJECT carry no value at all - so the rule is uniform across every tag and nothing here can fall out of step with that file. Which type a given tag carries is still pinned there and deliberately not restated here. NOTE THE CONTRAST with schemas/envelope-1.0.json's `record` property, which is NOT constrained this way and MUST NOT BE: a full copy carries the record in its original JSON form, numbers included, and there the parser requirement of spec section 6.4 is what protects the literals rather than the schema.

allOf.description: Recurse into an array, so a number cannot hide inside one.
Recurse into an object, so a number cannot hide inside one. This is what makes the constraint hold for the BLOB_REF carrier, whose blobByteLength is a nested member.

displayPath.description: Display only. Never hashed. STATED LIMIT: that is a rule about what an IMPLEMENTATION does with this string, not a constraint on the string, so no keyword here can express it and the implementation plus conformance class 6 own it. Spec section 5.2 gives the trap in full: reconstructing segments by parsing this form is what the structured encoding exists to make unnecessary.

input.description: Input in carrier form. Numbers are STRINGS here; a JSON number in a test vector would be parsed through a float by the very implementations under test. That is now enforced by the carrierValue reference rather than asserted in this sentence.

rejectVector.description: MUST error. An implementation that silently canonicalizes any of these is non-conformant.

input.description: The input that MUST error, in carrier form. A JSON NUMBER IS NOT A LEGITIMATE REJECTION INPUT, and this was considered rather than inherited: most of the class-3 rejection inputs are not valid JSON numbers in the first place - `01`, `1.`, `.5`, `+1`, `NaN` and `Infinity` cannot be written as JSON number tokens at all (docs/conformance-corpus.md class 3) - and the one that can, `1.4e+9999`, is precisely the case a float-based parser turns into Infinity before the runner ever hands it to the implementation under test, so writing it as a number would delete the vector's own subject. Carrying these as strings is not a workaround: spec section 6.4 requires an implementation to read a number's SOURCE BYTES rather than a parsed value, so the string IS the faithful representation of what the implementation is given.

leafVector.description: One leafHash over (path, tag, value, salt) per spec section 8. The salt is an INPUT here and nothing derives it: decision D4 is ruled D4b, so each salt is 16 bytes drawn independently from a CSPRNG (spec section 7). This definition replaced the deleted saltVector, which asserted that a (masterSalt, recordId, path) triple produced a given salt under a derivation that no longer exists.

value.description: The leaf's value in carrier form. Absent for the tags that carry none - NULL, EMPTY_ARRAY and EMPTY_OBJECT (spec section 6.1).

treeVector.description: RFC 9162 MTH over already-hashed leaves. Leaf counts 1,2,3,5,7,8,9,130 are mandatory (docs/conformance-corpus.md class 8): the RFC split rule is where a hand-rolled tree goes wrong. STATED LIMIT: that is a requirement on the SET of vectors, not on any one of them, so it is enforced by the corpus build alongside the class-coverage check classRef describes, and no per-vector keyword here can express it.

negativeProofVector.description: MUST NOT verify. Includes the internal-node-presented-as-leaf case, which is dogtag's C1 hazard (spec section 9.3). CAUTION - AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG. It said RFC 9162 rejects that case structurally because it is position-bound. It does not: RFC 9162 section 2.1.3.2 takes the tree size as an INPUT, so an attacker supplying both the leaf hash and the tree size can choose a shape that walks an internal node to the genuine root. Measured on an 8-leaf tree and reproduced on Node v22.21.0: MTH(L[0:4]) presented as the leaf at index 0, with a forged tree size of 2 and the audit path [MTH(L[4:8])], VERIFIES (spec section 11.1). What closes the case is the 0x00 leaf-domain byte together with spec section 10 step 1, which requires a verifier to recompute the leaf hash from the disclosed path, tag, value and salt and never to accept one. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RUNNER: these vectors MUST be driven through the full disclosed-copy verification path, not through a bare fold primitive. A runner handing a leaf hash straight to verifyInclusion is testing the primitive dogtag documents as proving nothing on its own (merkle.rs:86-91), and will record a pass for an implementation with no defence at all.

attack.description: forged-tree-size is the case the leafCount correction added: a treeSize the attacker chose, rather than the tree's real size, to place a node of his choosing where a leaf should be. leafCount is outside the root and is not authority (spec sections 11.1 and 11.3).

typeMapVector.description: Asserts that a given path under a given type map resolves to a given tag, fails closed, or that the MAP ITSELF is rejected. EXACTLY ONE of expectTag, expectFailClosed and expectMapRejected is required: with none the vector asserts nothing, and with more than one it asserts contradictory things. Every other vector type in this file requires its assertion, and class 11 is the highest-risk surface in the design (docs/conformance-corpus.md), so a silently vacuous vector is the worst place to allow one.

expectFailClosed.description: const true rather than a boolean, matching expectSameRoot and the three class-12 assertions in this file. A vector setting this to false asserted the negation of its own branch - the path IS covered - while naming no tag, which is the silently vacuous vector the oneOf above exists to forbid, reached from inside a branch instead of by omitting one.

expectMapRejected.description: const true, for the reason given on expectFailClosed. A vector asserting that the map is NOT rejected states nothing about what it resolves to.

oneOf.description: Asserts that the path is not covered and the implementation fails closed (spec section 4.2, decision D7 ruled D7a).

Asserts that the TYPE MAP is rejected outright rather than that a lookup within it fails. Added when decision D9 was ruled: a map binding any path to tag 8 BLOB_REF MUST be rejected, because the content-addressed binding is defined and selected by no version-1 profile (spec section 6.5). This is a different outcome from failing closed - the path IS covered, by a binding no profile has declared - and conflating the two would let an implementation pass by treating an undeclared binding as an unknown path.

recordVector.description: A whole record with its root. The three real MOH samples are mandatory (class 10). Records are referenced by file rather than inlined, so that no reference schema or sample is copied into this repository. EVERY input to the root that the protocol REQUIRES is required here, because the leaf set is the UNION of the record's leaves and the reserved roax.* leaves (spec sections 3.3 and 11.2): recordType, schemaVersion, recordId and issuerId are reserved-leaf values and therefore change the root, so a vector omitting any of them is not reproducible and the class-10 assertion would be untestable. The top-level canon and hashAlg supply the rest, via the domain string. THE PER-LEAF SALTS ARE THE REMAINING INPUT AND THE oneOf BELOW MAKES THEM STRUCTURALLY UNAVOIDABLE: decision D4 is ruled D4b, so every salt is an independent random draw that nothing can re-derive (spec section 7), and a vector that names only a bare record file asserts a root no runner can recompute. Under the deleted D4a construction a masterSaltHex plus recordId sufficed, which is why this used to be expressible as an optional field; it is not any more.

recordType.description: Committed as the reserved leaf roax.recordType, so it is an input to the root and not a label.

schemaVersion.description: Committed as the reserved leaf roax.schemaVersion. OPAQUE, exactly as in the envelope and for the same reason (spec section 12.1): defined by the profile rather than by this project, so it is matched for equality and never parsed.

issuerId.description: Committed as the reserved leaf roax.issuer.id.

issuerKeyId.description: Committed as the reserved leaf roax.issuer.keyId. OPTIONAL, and its ABSENCE is meaningful rather than a default: an absent issuerKeyId emits NO leaf, which changes both leafCount and root, and it MUST NOT be substituted with a NULL leaf or an empty string (spec section 11.2). A vector that omits this field asserts the no-leaf case.

recordFile.description: A BARE record file: the record body alone, carrying no salts. Usable only alongside saltsFile - see the oneOf below.

envelopeFile.description: A FULL envelope copy in the shape schemas/envelope-1.0.json defines, which carries the record body and its `salts` array together. A full copy MUST carry the salt of every leaf of the union (spec section 7.3), so this one file is self-sufficient and saltsFile would be a second, contradictable source of the same values.

saltsFile.description: The file carrying the per-leaf salts this vector's root was computed with, one per leaf of the union, in the `salts` shape schemas/envelope-1.0.json defines. REQUIRED alongside recordFile rather than optional, because a bare record file plus a root is not a reproducible assertion: every salt is an independent random draw that nothing can re-derive (spec section 7, decision D4 ruled D4b). This field replaced masterSaltHex, which expressed a derivation that no longer exists.

leafCount.description: The UNION count: the record's own leaves plus the 4 always-emitted reserved leaves, plus 1 when issuerKeyId is present. The floor is 5, because a record contributing zero leaves of its own MUST be rejected at issuance (spec section 3.3), and the if/then below raises it to 6 when issuerKeyId is present, because that case emits 5 reserved leaves rather than 4. STATED LIMIT, ENFORCED BY THE CORPUS BUILD RATHER THAN HERE: the floor is all a schema can check, because the record's own leaf count lives in the referenced file. The build MUST flatten that file, add the reserved leaves of spec section 11.2, and reject a vector whose leafCount disagrees, exactly as schemas/envelope-1.0.json records for the equivalent salts.length relationship.

if.description: An issuerKeyId means a fifth reserved leaf, so the union floor moves with it.

oneOf.description: A bare record file together with the salt set its root was computed under. Both are required: neither alone determines the root.

A full envelope copy, which already carries both. saltsFile is forbidden here rather than merely unnecessary: two carriers of the same salts can disagree, and a runner has no rule for which one the asserted root was computed under.

unlinkabilityVector.description: Class 12. Two records for the same subject, sharing a path AND a value at that path, MUST produce DIFFERENT leaf hashes for that path (spec section 7). This is the only vector class that catches an implementation whose salts are not independent, and that violation is invisible to every other class because each record verifies perfectly on its own. It has to catch three reachable mistakes, and the three assertions below map onto them one for one: a salt derived deterministically so that reissuance reproduces the same root, which reads like a feature; ONE DRAW REUSED ACROSS THE LEAVES OF A RECORD, which needs two DISTINCT paths compared WITHIN a single issuance and is why this vector carries a `paths` array rather than one `segments`; and one draw reused across records, which is the patient-linkage failure itself. THESE VECTORS ASSERT RELATIONS RATHER THAN PINNED VALUES, and that is forced by the ruling rather than a shortcut: decision D4 is ruled D4b, so the salts are independently random and no fixed expectation can exist for what the implementation under test must draw freshly. ONE TAG AND ONE VALUE ARE SHARED BY EVERY PATH rather than stated per path, which is what lets `paths` be a bare array of segment lists whose distinctness the schema can enforce with uniqueItems; it also makes the vector strictly stronger, because two leaves carrying the same tag and value at different paths additionally expose a salt derived from record content, which per-path values would mask. HONEST LIMIT: this detects a DETERMINISTIC or REUSED salt. It does NOT detect a weak or predictable CSPRNG - an implementation drawing 16 bytes from a poorly seeded generator passes every trial while providing far less than the 128 bits spec section 7 requires. No fixed vector file can test a randomness source; that gap belongs to implementation review and is stated in docs/conformance-corpus.md class 12 rather than left for a passing run to imply.

class.description: Always 12. Pinned rather than left to classRef's 1-to-19 range, because the class number is what the corpus build's coverage check counts: a class-12 vector mislabelled as any other class would mark THAT class covered by a vector testing nothing about it, and leave class 12 reading as a gap. The same silently-vacuous shape this file guards elsewhere, one level up.

paths.description: The paths to issue a leaf at, in EVERY trial. AT LEAST TWO, AND DISTINCT, and both halves are enforced here rather than described: an implementation that draws one salt per RECORD and reuses it across every leaf still produces a different salt at any single path in each trial, so a one-path vector passes while the unlinkability property decision D4b was chosen for is destroyed, and two entries naming the SAME path would let expectDistinctSaltsWithinIssuance assert distinctness over a path a record can hold only once. uniqueItems is EXACT here rather than partial, because the items are the structured segment lists themselves: two paths are equal exactly when their segment sequences are equal (spec section 5.1), and the display path is never involved (spec section 5.2). An earlier shape made these entries objects carrying a per-path tag and value, where uniqueItems compared whole objects and two entries sharing segments with different tags still validated. ONE RESIDUE THE RUNNER MUST ENFORCE IN CODE: two keys differing only in Unicode normalization form are unequal as JSON text and equal as paths once NFC is applied (spec section 6.1), so the corpus build MUST compare NFC-normalized segments and reject such a pair.

tag.description: The type tag bound at EVERY path in `paths`. One tag for the whole vector, because the class is about salt independence and nothing in it varies with the tag; tag variation is classes 1 and 7. STATED LIMIT, ENFORCED BY THE CORPUS BUILD RATHER THAN HERE: a tag is not a property of a vector but of a path under a type map, and resolution fails closed for an uncovered path (spec section 4.2, decision D7 ruled D7a), so this field is coherent only because a class-12 vector is issued against a SYNTHETIC record and a synthetic type map the build constructs, binding every entry in `paths` to this tag. No referenced MOH sample is involved and none could be, since the class needs two paths carrying one value. The build MUST construct that map and MUST reject a vector it cannot construct one for.

value.description: The value carried at EVERY path in `paths`, in carrier form as in encodeValueVector: numbers are STRINGS. Absent for the tags that carry no value - NULL, EMPTY_ARRAY and EMPTY_OBJECT (spec section 6.1). Carrying it once is what makes 'the same value at the same path in every trial' structurally true rather than an instruction a vector author could disregard.
value.$comment: WHICH type this tag carries is still not restated here, because that mapping is pinned per tag by schemas/envelope-1.0.json and a second copy could fall out of step. The carrierValue reference is a different claim and does not have that problem: no tag carries a JSON number under any of those conditionals, so the rule is uniform and copies no mapping.

recordIds.description: OPTIONAL. The record identifiers to issue the trials under, when the vector wants to pin that a SHARED identifier still yields different leaf hashes. Under decision D4b the record identifier is not an input to any salt or preimage, so this changes nothing about the expected outcome; it exists so a vector can state that explicitly, because the deleted derived-salt construction did fold it in and a reader who knows that construction would otherwise wonder.

trials.description: How many independent issuances the runner performs. Minimum 2, which is the pair the class is about; more raises confidence against an implementation that varies only the first draw.

expectDistinctSaltsWithinIssuance.description: Within EACH single trial, the salts drawn at the `paths` entries MUST all differ. This is the assertion that catches one draw reused across the leaves of a record (spec section 7, which requires each salt to be drawn independently and MUST NOT be reused across leaves), and it is the only one in this corpus that does, which is why the distinctness of `paths` is enforced by the schema rather than asked for in prose.

expectDistinctSaltsAcrossIssuances.description: At EACH path, the salt drawn in every trial MUST differ from the salt drawn at that same path in every other trial. This is the assertion that catches a deterministic salt and a salt reused across records.

expectDistinctLeafHashesAcrossIssuances.description: At EACH path, the leaf hash MUST differ across trials. This is the class's stated property expressed on the value a verifier actually sees. THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO within-issuance leaf-hash assertion: two leaves at different paths have different encoded paths inside the leaf preimage (spec section 8), so their hashes differ whether or not the salts do, and asserting it would read as coverage it is not.

normalizationVector.description: Class 19. One record whose string differs before and after NFC, carried in BOTH forms, asserting that the two produce the SAME root (spec section 6.1, decision D12 ruled D12a). Class 4 already asserts NFC against NFD at LEAF level in values and keys; this class asserts the property of the whole pipeline over the union of spec section 3.3, which is where the routes a leaf-level vector misses actually are - a key compared before normalization, a reserved-leaf value written straight from the envelope, a path segment re-encoded from a cached form. THE ASSERTION IS EQUALITY, so the vector is complete without a pinned root: what it fixes is that both forms yield one value and that it is the same one. The optional root pins that value once the corpus file exists, as a regression against normalization silently changing. Use a string whose NFC form is stable across recent Unicode versions - the version pin is class 16's subject, and class 16 is explicit about what it can and cannot demonstrate.

class.description: Always 19, pinned for the reason given on unlinkabilityVector.class.

site.description: Where the differing sequence sits. Both are required by docs/conformance-corpus.md class 19, because an implementation can normalize values and not keys. STATED LIMIT: that is a requirement on the SET of class-19 vectors and not on any one of them, so it is enforced by the corpus build alongside the class-coverage check classRef describes. It is left there rather than expressed as a pair of contains keywords on vectors.normalization, because that would half-enforce it - an absent array escapes entirely - and would make one class of nineteen carry its coverage rule in a different place from the other eighteen.

saltsFile.description: The per-leaf salts both forms are computed under, in the `salts` shape schemas/envelope-1.0.json defines. REQUIRED, and required structurally rather than as advice, for the same reason recordVector requires a salt source: under decision D4b every salt is an independent random draw (spec section 7), so two issuances of the two forms produce different roots for a reason that has nothing to do with normalization, and expectSameRoot would then assert nothing. The two forms MUST share one salt set.

root.description: OPTIONAL. The single root both forms produce, once computed.

envelopeVector.description: Classes 13-18: envelope and record-level invariants that JSON Schema alone cannot express, notably the minimum-disclosure floor (class 14), the reserved-namespace guard (class 15, which tests the NFC-normalized key of the FIRST SEGMENT for the prefix 'roax.' and is NOT a display-path test - see spec section 11.2), the prohibition on a disclosed copy carrying a withheld leaf's salt (class 17), and the outside-the-root authority vectors (class 18).

class.description: 13 to 18, matching the range this definition's own description states, and pinned for the reason given on unlinkabilityVector.class. The lower bound is where envelope-level invariants begin and the upper bound is class 18; the if/then/else below then splits 18 from 13 to 17.

verifierConfig.description: What the VERIFIER is configured with for this vector. Class 18 vectors are the only ones whose outcome depends on this rather than on the envelope alone, which is the whole point of the class: it fails an implementation that takes authority from a field in the document instead. Without this block the expected outcome of such a vector is not determined by the file, so the if/then/else on this definition REQUIRES it at class 18 and FORBIDS it everywhere else - it used to be optional with that requirement written only in this sentence, which made the check on the very class added to catch outside-the-root trust one that could not fail. THE FOUR MEMBERS ANY VERIFIER HAS ARE ALL REQUIRED - the anchored root, the anchored algorithm, the allow-list and the configured registry - which guards the same silently-vacuous-vector failure as the neighbouring typeMapVector's three-branch oneOf but more tightly: there the vector needs exactly one of three assertions, whereas a class-18 verifier configuration is under-determined unless every member is stated. The upper-edge ACCEPT vector of docs/conformance-corpus.md class 18 is the proof of that - it accepts only if the anchored pair matches, the algorithm is on the allow-list, and the registry read is the verifier's own, so a partial block would let it pass or fail for a reason the file did not fix. Decision D8 is ruled with this class attached to it, because a normative sentence alone was demonstrably not enough - dogtag had the equivalent understanding written down and still shipped the documentStore bug (spec section 11.3).

anchoredRoot.description: The root the verifier's own anchoring registry records. Authority for the root comes from here, never from the envelope.

anchoredHashAlg.description: The hash algorithm the registry records against that root. A verifier MUST take hashAlg from HERE and never from the envelope (spec section 7.4, H2). A vector whose envelope hashAlg disagrees with this value MUST be rejected.

hashAlgAllowList.description: The algorithms this verifier is configured to accept. Closes the retired-algorithm case that the registry alone does not (spec section 7.4, H3): a vector whose algorithm is registered but absent from this list MUST be rejected. A DISCRIMINATING H3 vector sets this to ["Poseidon-BN254"] against a SHA-256 envelope, because that is the only shape in which an implementation with no allow-list at all fails; a Poseidon envelope is rejected anyway for having no defined construction (spec section 7.4), so a vector built the other way round records a pass without an allow-list existing. Minimum one entry: a verifier configured with an empty list rejects everything, and every vector run against it would then pass for that reason instead of the one it names.

registryAddress.description: The anchoring registry the verifier is configured with. An envelope naming a DIFFERENT registry in its anchor block MUST NOT cause the verifier to read that one - this is the dogtag documentStore bug in this design's shape. An absent anchor block MUST NOT make an otherwise verifiable record unverifiable, which is the accept vector at the upper edge of class 18.

registryChainId.description: OPTIONAL, and the one member of this block that is: a registry on a chain without a numeric identifier has none to state, whereas the other four exist for every verifier. The class-18 vector whose envelope names a registry the verifier is not configured with SHOULD state it when the registry has one, because the anchor block carries both an address and a chain identifier and a verifier must ignore both.

then.description: Class 18 is the outside-the-root authority class, so the verifier's own configuration is half of what determines the outcome and the file must state it.

else.description: Every other class in 13-17 is determined by the envelope alone, so a verifierConfig here would be inert and would suggest the outcome turns on something it does not.
